study.question: Under exactly the same supplied causal history, does retaining four action-specific target-aware summaries improve information retention relative to equally wide interleaved summaries, and does within-group attention normalization account for any gain?
study.hypothesis: Observation: baseline-static AUC=0.6050036144838207, baseline-pooled=0.6102261137080656, baseline-din=0.6133619861190683 on 3234051 validation impressions; corresponding Logloss=0.19725549413961715, 0.19708646342353378, 0.19679464647483236. DIN minus pooled AUC=0.0031358724110027, but these are single-seed receipts, not uncertainty estimates. Source inspection shows that the reference first sums category, brand, action and recency embeddings, then compresses all events into one 16D global-softmax summary. This is a concrete representational bottleneck; useful information loss and rare-action dilution are unverified explanations. Provisional mechanism: retaining action identity in separate downstream slots may expose complementary evidence that is difficult to decode from a mixed vector; normalizing inside each action may additionally protect sparse groups from global competition. Existing long-history slice (3026583 impressions, 151372 positives, 2875211 negatives) improves from pooled AUC 0.6112561436467834 to DIN 0.61442034774157; short-history improvements also occur. This motivates investigating representation but does not diagnose action dilution. Composition slices show overlapping action presence: pv=3223053, cart=2111110, fav=1179004, buy=1888339 out of 3234051; these impression-presence counts do not establish per-event frequency or complementary utility. The three available trajectories all succeeded; there are no supplied failed branches or prior mechanism candidates, previous_runtime_error is null, and scoped-memory search returned no records. Starting-point verification: baseline_reference.py, initial candidate.py and history_baseline_din.py share SHA256 ee10868f589c077b19f57a1fb07702c947c56e970994cdc537ef83ea2b8bc943, matching the authorized receipt. Raw physical tables, host causal audit and checkpoints are not available here; no new execution or data-integrity result is claimed.

Full author implementation and training techniques are not reproduced.

study.proposed_difference: A 2x2 factorial: partition by actual history_type versus valid-event ordinal modulo four; normalize shared event scores globally versus independently within each group. Concatenate four 16D summaries to the unchanged static features, giving 64D history input in every new cell. True action embeddings remain present even in position controls. All four source modules are identical and independently executable with their proposal configs; they have exactly the same parameter tensors and initialization order. At the frozen dimensions, each adds 3*16*128=6144 first-layer weights over baseline-din, for an analytic expected total 17136419 and dense count 57731, pending host measurement. Both normalization paths are computed and combined with a fixed 0/1 coefficient in every cell; no optimizer or loss intervention. Empty and absent groups are zero. This tests retaining explicit group evidence and competition geometry; it does not disaggregate category and brand within each event, extend history, build graphs, or establish novelty. Model.diagnostics returns 24 named scalars on the fixed first-512 host sample: visible counts, occupancy, global/selected attention mass, summary RMS and true-action counts. This small convenience sample is exploratory only, not population slice evidence.
predictions: Primary confirmatory screening contrast: behavior_within AUC exceeds interleaved_within under paired seed 42. Repeat the main candidate and closest controls with seeds 43 and 44 before claiming repeated support; no significance claim from the first run.

If action identity matters independently of normalization, behavior_global also exceeds interleaved_global. If normalization and semantic groups interact, the predeclared difference-of-differences is positive across paired seeds.

Within-group selected attention mass is exactly 1 for each present slot and 0 for absent slots; global total attention mass is 1 for nonempty histories and 0 for empty histories. These are implementation diagnostics, not performance or causal-mechanism evidence.

Report all frozen history-length and behavior-presence slices with host sample/positive/negative counts. A gain concentrated where multiple actions are present would be exploratory support; current overlapping presence slices cannot by themselves establish this pattern.

All four variants have identical parameter counts. Four-slot aggregation adds O(B*4*L*D) work without changing event encoding/scoring order O(B*L); both normalization paths incur deliberate control overhead. Any measured AUC gain must be shown with wall/GPU time, peak memory, examples processed, throughput and batch p50/p95 latency.
Full AUC and Logloss may move differently. A higher AUC with worse calibration will be reported as a tradeoff; the existing full-population AUC remains the frozen selection metric.
falsifiers: If behavior slots do not outperform same-width position controls under either normalization across paired seeds, these implementations provide no controlled support for an action-specific advantage. A gain only versus the narrower baseline is insufficient.

If within-group gains also occur comparably in position controls, or disappear at global normalization, reject a standalone action-semantics explanation and retain generic reweighting or interaction as alternatives.

If rare-action global mass is not small in the exploratory diagnostics, do not claim the proposed dilution observation has been verified. Even small mass plus a gain is not enough to identify dilution as the unique causal explanation.

If attention masks fail to cover each valid event once, outputs are nonfinite, empty histories produce nonzero summaries, or parameter counts differ across cells, stop and repair with charged failure receipts before interpreting scores.

If no new cell improves the measured quality-cost frontier or any cell exceeds the frozen cap, do not claim efficiency; retain baseline-din when appropriate. One capped/failed implementation does not refute the abstract grouping hypothesis.
alternative_explanations: True-action slots and position slots have different occupancy, event content and count imbalance; this is part of the partition intervention, so it does not isolate semantic identity from occupancy.
Interleaving preserves four position phases and may exploit supplied history order. It is a useful active-capacity replacement, not a pure exchangeability or random-label null.

Within-group normalization changes attention mass, relative group scale, frequency information and gradient allocation together; a positive contrast supports that intervention, not a unique rare-action-dilution explanation.

Nominal capacity and operator graph match across the four new variants; effective representational capacity and measured kernel cost can still differ. All four add 6144 dense parameters over baseline-din.
One seed and one temporal validation split are preliminary. Existing slice AUCs have unequal composition; no per-example uncertainty or significance is inferred from aggregate receipts.
Shared field-sum encoding may be the dominant bottleneck, so an unsuccessful action-slot intervention need not imply event information is adequate.
Training dynamics, sparse parameter updates and selection among four cells can produce apparent validation gains; preserve all cells and report seed variation and selection scope.
Publisher static user/ad snapshot as-of times are undocumented. The benchmark treats them as static; this limitation is inherited and cannot be repaired by modifying the frozen input contract.

variants.name: behavior_within
variants.note: Main candidate: one target-aware, separately normalized 16D slot per true action; concatenate four slots. Compare primarily with interleaved_within, then behavior_global. Same visible events as baseline-din; no extra raw fields or labels.

variants.name: interleaved_within
variants.note: Replacement control: four slots by valid-event ordinal modulo four, retaining true action embeddings. Same parameter tensors, scorer, head, softmax paths, data and training as behavior_within. Position is supplied order, not a random seed intervention.

variants.name: behavior_global
variants.note: Normalization ablation: preserve four true-action slots but allocate event weights with a single global softmax. Summing these slots recovers the reference global history summary algebraically for fixed embeddings/scorer.

variants.name: interleaved_global
variants.note: Fourth factorial cell: interleaved slots and global normalization; controls the true-action partition at global normalization and supplies its within-group-normalization contrast.

knowledge_assessments.rationale: Retrieved via tools.py search behavior. Organizer summary raises complementary-group and compression questions, but supplies no isolated effects; local reference code and receipts motivate this study independently. True action types are not business domains, and per-event composition/recency utility is not yet measured.
knowledge_assessments.transformed_mechanism: No adoption of dual old/recent paths, domain exchange or gates. Four shared-scorer slots are a simpler local intervention; analogy is not evidence of transfer.
knowledge_assessments.nearest_work_difference: The proposed factorial compares action grouping and normalization without a compression path or cross-domain feedback. No reproduction claim or component-level source verification is made.
knowledge_assessments.falsifier: No repeated action-partition gain over interleaved controls would reject the local complementarity implementation; it would not refute the unreproduced external system.
